## **Previously on 201**
<br>
- defining the meaning of words **by sense** and **by reference**:
  - a word's **sense** is the **mental concept** of the word's meaning or a dictionary definition of the word's meaning
  - a word's **reference** is the set of entities (referents) that the word **refers to**<br><br>
- consider the word <i><u>university</u></i>
  - **sense**: an institution of higher education
  - **reference**: Rutgers, NYU, CUNY, Harvard, MIT, Penn, Stanford, Johns Hopkins...<br><br>

- **Semantics** is the study of **literal** meaning in language
  - lexical semantics (words) and compositional semantics (sentences)<br><br>

- lexical meaning is **conventional** and **arbitrary**
  - under this, we can have different relations: synonym, antonynm, hypernym, hyponym<br><br>

- compositional meaning includes **truth values** of the sentence
  - sentences can have multiple propositions with different **truth values**

# **ENTAILMENT** <br><br>

### a proposition ***p*** entails another proposition ***q*** <span style="color:green"><b>if</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>whenever</b></span> ***p*** is <span style="color:black; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>, ***q*** must also be <span style="color:black; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span><br><br>

### more formally: ***p*** entails ***q*** <span style="color:green"><b>iff whenever</b></span> ***p*** is <span style="color:black; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>, ***q*** is <span style="color:black; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span><br><br>

<span style="color:green"><b>iff</b></span>: if and only if<br><br>
"<span style="color:green"><b>whenever</b></span>": it means you cannot find any possible world, 
where **q** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>false</b></span> while **p** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>

## **Entailment**
<br>
.pull-left[
.pull-left[<img src="../pic/1021/earth.png" width="100%">]
.pull-right[]
.pull-left[]
.pull-right[<img src="../pic/1021/snoopy.png" width="100%">]
]
.pull-right[
the relationship between the propositions in a sentence is called **entailment**<br><br>
- a proposition ***p*** entails another proposition ***q*** <span style="color:green"><b>if</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>whenever</b></span> ***p*** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>, ***q*** must also be <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span><br><br>

let's say we have two propositions<br><br>
<b><i>p:</i></b> <span style="color:deeppink"><i><u>Snoopy is a beagle.</u></i></span><br>
<b><i>q:</i></b> <span style="color:teal"><i><u>Snoopy is a dog.</u></i></span><br><br>
proposition <b><i>p</i></b> **entails** proposition <b><i>q</i></b><br><br>
because if we say "<span style="color:deeppink"><i><u>Snoopy is a beagle.</u></i></span>" is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>,<br>
Snoopy must be a dog, since beagles are dogs,<br>
then "<span style="color:teal"><i><u>Snoopy is a dog.</u></i></span>" is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span><br><br>
But, <b><i>q</i></b> does NOT **entail** <b><i>p</i></b>, why?
]

## **Entailment and Possible Words**
<br>
.pull-left[
- recall our definition of **entailment**<br><br>
**entailment**: a proposition ***p*** entails another proposition ***q*** <span style="color:green"><b>if</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>whenever</b></span> ***p*** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>, ***q*** must also be <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span><br><br>
**in other words**: ***p*** entails ***q*** when there is <span style="color:blue"><b>NO</b></span> possible world in which ***p*** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span> and ***q*** is <span style="color:green; font-variant: small-caps"><b>false</b></span><br><br><br>

(a) Merlin has a fluffy dog.<br><br>
(b) Merlin has a dog.<br><br>
(c) Merlin has a fluffy dog and a cat.
]
.pull-right[
<br><br>
- (a) **entails** (b) because (a) cannot be <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span> while (b)
is <span style="color:green; font-variant: small-caps"><b>false</b></span>:<br><br>
  - there is <span style="color:blue"><b>NO</b></span> possible world in which<br>
  <i><u>Merlin has a fluffy dog but not a dog</u></i><br><br>
- (b) does <span style="color:blue"><b>NOT</b></span> **entail** (a) because (b) can be <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>
while (a) is <span style="color:green; font-variant: small-caps"><b>false</b></span>:<br><br>
  - there is a possible world, in which <br>
  <i><u>Merlin could have a short-haired dog</u></i><br><br>
- (c) **entails** both (a) and (b) because (c) cannot be <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span> while (a) or (b) is <span style="color:green; font-variant: small-caps"><b>false</b></span>
]

---
.pull-left[
## **Entailment**
<br>
consider the following sentences:<br><br>
(a) Alicia drank coffee at midnight.<br><br>
(b) Alicia drank coffee.<br><br>
(c) Alicia drank coffee at midnight in the living room.<br><br>
]
.pull-right[
<br><br>
**entailment**: a proposition ***p*** entails another proposition ***q*** <span style="color:green"><b>if</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>whenever</b></span> ***p*** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>, ***q*** must also be <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span><br><br>
**in other words**: ***p*** entails ***q*** when there is <span style="color:blue"><b>NO</b></span> possible world in which ***p*** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span> and ***q*** is <span style="color:green; font-variant: small-caps"><b>false</b></span>
]
.pull-left[
- does (a) **entail** (b)?<br><br>
- does (a) **entail** (c)?<br><br>
- does (b) **entail** (c)?<br><br>
- does (c) **entail** (a)?
]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1021/sor.gif" style="width:50%;">
</div>
]

---
.pull-left[
## **Entailment**
<br>
consider the following sentences:<br><br>
(a) Alicia drank coffee at midnight.<br><br>
(b) Alicia drank coffee.<br><br>
(c) Alicia drank coffee at midnight in the living room.<br><br>
]
.pull-right[
<br><br>
**entailment**: a proposition ***p*** entails another proposition ***q*** <span style="color:green"><b>if</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>whenever</b></span> ***p*** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span>, ***q*** must also be <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span><br><br>
**in other words**: ***p*** entails ***q*** when there is <span style="color:blue"><b>NO</b></span> possible world in which ***p*** is <span style="color:#CC0033; font-variant: small-caps"><b>true</b></span> and ***q*** is <span style="color:green; font-variant: small-caps"><b>false</b></span><br><br><br>
]

- does (a) **entail** (b)? <span style="color:blue"><i>yes: if Alicia drank coffee at midnight is true, it must be true that Alicia drank coffee</i></span><br><br>
- does (a) **entail** (c)? <span style="color:green"><i>no: Suppose Alicia drank coffee at midnight in the kitchen. (a) will be true while (b) is false</i></span><br><br>
- does (b) **entail** (c)? <span style="color:green"><i>no: Suppose Alicia drank coffee in the morning. (b) will be true while (c) is false</i></span><br><br>
- does (c) **entail** (a)? <span style="color:blue"><i>yes: If Alicia drank coffee at midnight in the living room is true, it must be true that
Alicia drank coffee at midnight</i></span>

---
## **Logical Entailment**<br><br>
.pull-left[
- **p** *entails* **q** for logical reasons, **regardless** of world knowledge or lexical meaning <br><br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>The cat sat on the mat.</b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>There is a cat/mat.</b></span> <br><br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>(a dog): I heard the can opener.</b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>(Therefore for the dog), FOOD EXISTS!.</b></span> <br><br>
- We got the entailment relation between **p** and **q** by logical inferences
]
.pull-right[
<img src="../pic/1021/entail1.png" width="75%">
]

---
## **World-specific Entailment**<br><br>
.pull-left[
- **p** *entails* **q** due to <span style="color:green">world knowledge</span> or <span style="color:green">lexical meaning</span><br><br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>Charles III is the King of the United Kingdom.</b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>Queen Elizabeth II was Charles's mother.</b></span> <br><br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>Merlin is from Scotland. </b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>Merlin is from UK.</b></span> <br><br>
- We got the entailment relation between **p** and **q** by making reference to how the world works, or to knowledge of lexical meaning
]
.pull-right[
<img src="../pic/1021/entail3.png" width="75%">
]

---
## **Mutual Entailment**<br><br>
.pull-left[
- **p** *entails* **q** <span style="color:green"><b>AND</b></span> **q** *entails* **p** as well.<br><br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>Merlin is a sorcerer.</b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>Merlin is a wizard.</b></span> <br><br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>Merlin is immortal </b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>Merlin is not capable of dying.</b></span> <br><br>
]
.pull-right[
<img src="../pic/1021/entail4.png" width="75%">
]

.pull-right[
<br><br><br>
<h3><b><span style="color:#CC0033">TRANSITIVITY</span></b></h3><br><br>
a property where a **relation** transfers across elements<br><br>
for instance, **if** A=B and B=C, **then** A=C<br><br>
generally it refers to a "**passing over**" of a relationship, action, or property across elements
]

---
## **Entailment Notes I**
<br>
- importantly, not all entailment relations can be identified so easily from the **syntactic structure** of the sentences and/or the **particular words** that they contain <br><br>

.pull-left[
- consider three pairs of sentences below:<br><br>
(a). <i>Arthur <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>managed to</b></span> <span style="color:blue">leave</span> on time</i>.<br>
(b). <i>Arthur <span style="color:blue">left</span> on time</i>.<br><br>
(c). <i>Arthur <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>tried to</b></span> <span style="color:blue">leave</span> on time</i>.<br>
(d). <i>Arthur <span style="color:blue">left</span> on time</i>.<br><br>
(e). <i>Arthur <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>attempted to</b></span> <span style="color:blue">leave</span> on time</i>.<br>
(f). <i>Arthur <span style="color:blue">left</span> on time</i>.<br><br>

1. does (a) **entail** (b)? 
2. does (c) **entail** (d)? 
3. does (e) **entail** (f)? 
]

--

.pull-right[
<div style="text=align:center">
<h3>
in fact, <u>syntactic structure is a poor indicator of entailment</u>
<br><br>
after all, entailment is a <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>semantic relation</b></span>, not a syntactic one
</h3
</div>
]

---
## **Entailment Notes II: 'Weird' Case - Tautology**
<br>
- there are sentences that are **ALWAYS** true and they are **true** in every possible world (**tautology**)<br><br>
  - (a) <i>A dog is a dog</i>.<br><br>
  - (b) <i>I will either save the world or I will not save the world</i>.<br><br>

- given our definition of entailment, such sentences are **entailed by all other sentences**<br><br>
  - (c) <i>Merlin is a musical actor</i>.<br><br>
  
- (a) and (b) are **always** true, so whenever (c) is true, they will be true:
  - if Merlin **IS** actually a musical actor in a possible world, then "<i>A dog is a dog</i>." is **true**<br><br>

- we call this: entailment holds **vacuously**
  - why we call it "vacuously"?

# **PRESUPPOSITION** <br><br>
### A **SPECIAL** TYPE OF ENTAILMENT <br><br>

___

### for two propositions <span style="color:green"><b>p</b></span> and <span style="color:blue"><b>q</b></span>:<br><br>
###<span style="color:green"><b>p</b></span> presupposes <span style="color:blue"><b>q</b></span> iff **both** <span style="color:green"><b>p</b></span> and the <span style="color:deeppink"><b>negation</b></span> of <span style="color:green"><b>p</b></span> **entail** <span style="color:blue"><b>q</b></span>

---
## **Presupposition: a Special Type of Entailment**
<br>
- consider the following two pairs of sentences:<br><br>

(a). <i>My brother Jeong Kwan lives in Korea</i>.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;(c). <i>My brother Jeong Kwan <span style="color:green"><b>does not</b></span> live in Korea</i>.<br><br>

(b). <i><span style="color:#CC0033">I have a brother</span></i>.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
(b). <i><span style="color:#CC0033">I have a brother</span></i>.<br><br>

.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
does (a) entail (b)?
</div>
]

.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:left">
does (c) entail (b)?
</div>
]<br><br>

--

- this entailment **survives negation** so it is also a **presupposition**<br><br>

--

- "if it is a <b><span style="color:blue">presupposition</span></b> relation, it must be an <b><span style="color:green">entailment</span></b> relation as well"
- "if it is an <b><span style="color:green">entailment</span></b> relation, it is <b><span style="color:deeppink">NOT necessarily</span></b> a <b><span style="color:blue">presuppostion</span></b> relation"<br><br>

--

we also say that a <b><span style="color:blue">presuppostion</span></b> is the <u>belief or background (tacit) assumption</u> whose truth is <span style="color:#CC0033">taken for
granted</span> in a sentence or discourse

---
## **Presupposition: a Special Type of Entailment**
<br>
- **FOR INSTANCE**:<br><br>

.pull-left[
(a). <i><span style="color:blue">Merlin drank coffee</span> <span style="color:green">in the library</span></i>.<br><br>
(b). <i><span style="color:blue">Merlin drank coffee</span></i>.
]
.pull-right[
(c). <i><span style="color:blue">Merlin <span style="color:deeppink">DID NOT</span> drink coffee</span> <span style="color:green">in the library</span></i>.<br><br>
(b). <i><span style="color:blue">Merlin drank coffee</span></i>.
]<br><br>

--

.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
(a) <span style="color:#CC0033">entails</span>  (b)
</div>
]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
(c) <span style="color:deeppink">does NOT</span> <span style="color:#CC0033">entail</span>  (b)
</div>
]
<br><br>
- therefore, (a) is <span style="color:deeppink">NOT</span> a **presupposition** of (b)<br><br>

--

- note here: we are deciding the presupposition relation between **proposition (a) and (b)**
- however, given our definition of presupposition, we have to refer to another proposition, **c**, which is the **negation of b,** to determine presupposition relation

---
.pull-left[
### **Exercise IV: Presupposition**
]
.pull-right[
**presupposition**: for two propositions <span style="color:green"><b>p</b></span> and <span style="color:blue"><b>q</b></span>, <span style="color:green"><b>p</b></span> presupposes <span style="color:blue"><b>p</b></span> iff **both** <span style="color:green"><b>p</b></span> and the <span style="color:deeppink"><b>negation</b></span> of <span style="color:green"><b>p</b></span> **entail** <span style="color:blue"><b>q</b></span>.
]
<br><br>
.pull-left[
do following pairs of sentence fall under **presupposition** relation?<br><br>
(1)<br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>The cat sat on the mat.</b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>There is a cat/mat.</b></span> <br><br>
(2)<br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>(a dog): I heard the can opener.</b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>(Therefore for the dog), FOOD EXISTS!.</b></span> <br><br>
(3)<br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>The king of the United States is bald.</b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>There is a king of the United States.</b></span> <br><br>
(4)<br>
**p**: <span style="color:green"><b>Arthur is driving a blue car.</b></span> <br>
**q**: <span style="color:blue"><b>Arthur is driving a car.</b></span>
]
.pull-right[
**entailment**: Sentence **p** entails sentence **q** <span style="color:green"><b>iff</b></span><br>
**q** is true whenever **p** is true.
<br><br><br>

]
